caption: The drawing features two primary objects rendered in black ink lines on a light tan background. On the left side, there is a detailed side elevation of a three-legged tripod table, with proportions and measurements included. The tabletop is round with a 31-inch diameter, supported by a central spindle and an ornate turned segment above three curved legs, each extending outward and downward with claw-like feet. The total height to the tabletop is 27½ inches, with 9¾ inches from the spindle base to the foot. The leg spread is shown as 13½ inches across. Dotted lines indicate the swung-up, upright position of the tabletop when not in use. On the right side of the drawing is a square top-down view labeled “VIEW OF SPINDLE,” measuring 7⅝ inches per side; it contains five circles, one large at the center and four smaller ones at each corner. The composition also includes handwritten text at the top and bottom providing context, location (Corbin House at Edenton, NC, 1758), instructions about the table's swing mechanism, and identifying the drawing as a working drawing of the tripod table by Arthur Johnson, number 17907.
title: Tripod Table
